This appeal by the insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 07.10.2016 passed by 4th Additional MACT, Khargone (WN) in Claim Case No.231/2014 on the ground of false implication of offending vehicle for seeking compensation by the claimants.

2. Brief facts of the case are that respondent no.1 and 2 claimants filed a claim petition before the Tribunal on 10.07.2013 and pleaded that deceased Biharilal and Haresingh were travelling on their motorcycle on 26.02.2013 when on the way the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration no.MP-0536 which was being driven rashly and negligently hit the motorcycle resulting in grievous injuries to Biharilal who thereafter succumbed to his injuries.
3. Respondents No.3 & 4 who are driver and owner of the said offending vehicle filed their written statement and denied all the averments pleaded in the claim petition.
Appellant/insurance company also filed the written statement and denied all the averments.

4. Tribunal framed the issues on the basis of the pleading of both the parties and after taking the evidence of both the parties and hearing the counsel of both the parties allowed the claim petition in favour of respondents No.1 & 2 and awarded a compensation of Rs.32,37,952/- in their favour and against the appellant/insurance company.

Appellant/insurance company has filed this appeal on the ground that Tribunal has grossly erred in not considering that respondent No.1/claimant had filed New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Savitri Bai on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27900812/

sentences.text: late FIR after 23 days of the accident and no reasonable cause has been shown for filing late FIR.

Haresingh (AW/3), injured in his cross examination has specifically admitted that he was not unconscious at the time of accident, however after reaching hospital he did not disclose the number of the offending vehicle and the manner in which the accident took place.
There is no reasonable cause to file the delayed FIR.
The offending vehicle has been falsely implicated for seeking compensation.
He has further submitted that eye witness Haresingh has denied the involvement of insured vehicle in the criminal case.

In criminal case Haresingh has given contradictory statement due to which finding which has been recorded by the Tribunal holding the accident caused by the insured vehicle is contrary to the evidence.
Therefore, prayed for exonerating the insurance company from its liability to pay compensation.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents has supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of this appeal.
6. Claimants' counsel filed a cross objection for enhancement of compensation but during arguments he has not pressed the said cross objection, so the cross objection is dismissed as not pressed.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
8.

Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that FIR was lodged with delay and the said delay has not been properly explained but perusal of the record Ex.P/4 of Gokuldas hospital it was found that deceased Biharilal was admitted in Gokuldas hospital, Indore on 26.02.2013 and he died on 13.03.2013 during treatment in hospital.
Perusal of Nakshapanchayatnama Ex.P/7 it was found that in the opinion of the witnesses accident had occurred due to motor vehicle accident.
9. It was clear from the FIR Ex.P/2 that accident occurred on 26.02.2013 and FIR was lodged on 19.03.2013.

It is settled principle that although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the sa me should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.

10. The apex Court in the case of Ravi vs. Badirnarayan and others AIR 2011 SC 1226 in para-20 &
21 has held as under:
[20] It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.

entities.text: Ravi vs. Badirnarayan and others AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so;
the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Savitri Bai on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27900812/

sentences.text: then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
[21] The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.
11. It reveals that as per record date of accident was 26.02.2013.
It is clear from the Lash Nakshapanchayatnama that the accident was occurred due to motor vehicle accident.

Ordinarily,
after the accident if a family member of the claimants has died, we cannot expect that first they rush to the police station and lodge the report immediately after the accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupied in mind are that they give more importance to the victim's treatment rather than to rush.
So in the present case also, the family members of the deceased were naturally busy in the hospital for his treatment.
So in the considered opinion of this Court the delay in lodging the FIR is reasonable, therefore, on the basis of the said delay in filing the FIR, the claim case cannot be discarded.

12. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that eye witness Haresingh has given different versions in the claim case as well as criminal court, due to which finding has been recorded by the Tribunal that the accident was caused by an insured vehicle which is contrary to evidence placed on record.

He has further submitted that he filed documents, statement of Haresingh before the criminal court but statement deposed by Haresingh before the criminal court is not confronted him before the Tribunal.

13. In the case of Gautam vs. R.N.Singh - AIR 2008 MP 68, it is held that it is settled proposition of law that every civil case is decided on its own facts and evidence without influencing the papers and decision of the criminal case.
In such premises, registration of the offence and police investigation is not a condition precedent for awarding the claim.
14. In the case of P.Varalakshmi Reddy vs. Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation - 2003 ACJ 1952 (DB), it is held that Tribunal is not bind by the finding of criminal case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

15. In the present case, from the evidence adduced in claim case before the Tribunal it is found that driver of the offending vehicle was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently and hit the motorcycle New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Savitri Bai on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27900812/
4 of the deceased due to which the deceased received grievous injuries on his various parts of body and died.

sentences.text: The perusal of the record of the Tribunal it is found that the driver of the offending vehicle was present before the Tribunal but he did not dare to adduce any evidence or rebut the evidence produced by the claimants, so a presumption can be drawn against him.
It is also settled principle that acquittal of the accused in criminal case arising out of motor accident cases does not absolve him from the liability of compensation in claim cases.
16. In view of the foregoing discussion, in the considered opinion of this Court, it is not proved that the claimants have falsely implicated the offending vehicle for seeking compensation.
Hence, the appeal being devoid of merit and substance is hereby dismissed.
